newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine budget to be passed by end June-committee.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine budget to be passed by end June-committee.

text.p: The head of the Ukrainian parliament's budget committee said on Tuesday the five-month overdue 1997 budget would be passed by the end of this month.

"I predict that we will pass the budget around the last week of June. Once we get the final draft, deputies will require about two weeks to give it a second (final) reading," Mykola Azarov told Reuters.
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) is waiting to grant a $2.5 to $3 billion long-term credit once Ukraine passes the budget and a package of tax reform laws to underpin it.
Parliamentary speaker Alexander Moroz told deputies the government would hand the draft over to parliament on June 5.

"At a meeting yesterday the Finance Minister told the heads of parliament's committees and parties that the government had passed a resolution to finish the draft budget and give it to parliament for review on Thursday," Moroz said.
Moroz said parliament could begin debating the draft next week -- and would at the same time give preliminary approval to an initial draft of the 1998 budget.
Government and parliament have blamed each other for the record-long delay of the budget, which parliament initially approved last December and returned to government for revisions.
Parliament has voted to to start its summer recess on July 18.

The first deputy Finance Minister said last week the budget forecast gross domestic product at 100.4 billion hryvnias (54.6 billion) and the deficit was forecast at 5.7 percennt of gdp, compared to 6.2 percent in 1996.
It also forecast annual inflation at 24.9 percent, against 39.7 percent last year.
This year marks the longest period the budget has been delayed since independence in 1991. It was due on January 1 under Ukrainian law.
